chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who prays the obligatory prayer in which recitation is done aloud; is he required not to do so aloud? He said: 'If he wishes, he does so aloud, and if he wishes, he does not.'
This report is consistent with the general public (Sunni scholars) because they are the ones who allow choice in this matter, and what we act upon is what we have previously mentioned.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the Imam makes the recitation audible in the Friday prayer until the mention of 'and whoever missed the night prayer.' We will mention that in its chapters, if Allah the Exalted wills. Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever missed the night prayer, he makes it up in the first part of the day; if that does not suit him, he makes it up on the second night before its time, from the end of the night. And if he makes it up after the last Isha prayer before he sleeps, that suffices him. And likewise whoever missed the voluntary prayers of the day and was occupied with them, he makes them up at night; and if that misses him, he makes them up on the following day during the daytime.

key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the general public (often referring to Sunni scholars)
key_terms.صَدْرِ النَّهَارِ: the first part of the day
key_terms.قَضَاهَا: he made it up / compensated for it
key_terms.يُجْهَرُ: to make audible / to recite aloud

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up missed night prayers and voluntary day prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic flexibility (ikhtiyar) in reciting aloud or silently during audible obligatory prayers, contrasting the Shia view with the broader Sunni consensus. Al-Sheikh al-Tusi further elaborates on the temporal rules for qada (compensation) of missed night prayers and voluntary day prayers, establishing a structured hierarchy for making up missed acts of worship. This reflects the Shia emphasis on precise timing and intentionality in fulfilling religious obligations.
